subject: Enablement heatmap + release sequencing — clarify product asks and exception lanes
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, AtlasHealth Ops <ops@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Enablement heatmap + release sequencing — clarify product asks and exception lanes

Team,

We need to lock a few decisions this week so the AtlasHealth pilot can proceed without last-minute scope churn. Attached is a draft enablement heatmap and a dependency diagram (enablement-heatmap-v1.xlsx, seq-dependency-map.drawio). High-level asks from Product that need owners and acceptance criteria: 

1) Model pinning: Product asks we serve model v2.1 for the pilot and avoid mixed-model rollouts. Impact: infra needs a fallback plan if v2.1 causes regressions. Owner: Marcus?

2) SLA/latency doc: Provide a one-page SLO summary for Dedicated and Hosted modes (95th/99th token latency expectations). Owner: Monica + Infra.

3) Enablement: two 45-minute customer webinars, one technical quickstart doc, and three short troubleshooting KB articles. Owner: Lauren, with support from Docs.

Proposed sequencing: soft pilot release (limited to AtlasHealth) —> July 10 wide availability. If we hit compliance blockers from AtlasHealth, we should keep pilot running an extra two weeks rather than rush a wide release.

Questions / exception lanes I want clarity on by EOD Friday: 
- What constitutes a doc showstopper vs deferred doc work?
- What SLA deltas require an exception and who signs off?
- If model v2.1 causes a correctness regression, what fallback policy do we prefer (immediate revert, gradual traffic shift, or force to v1.9)?

Please reply with confirmed owners, dates, and any constraints. If you can’t commit to the proposed July 10 wide-release date, propose the latest safe date with rationale. AtlasHealth, please flag any compliance items we should treat as gating.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
VP, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: enablement-heatmap-v1.xlsx, seq-dependency-map.drawio
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, AtlasHealth Ops <ops@atlashealth.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Enablement heatmap + release sequencing — clarify product asks and exception lanes

Vanessa,

Thanks for the clear list. Quick notes from Docs/Enablement POV: 

- I can own the one-page SLO summary but need final latency numbers from Infra by Thursday EOD (we can draft with estimates but must mark them as provisional).
- The technical quickstart is currently at 40% — we can finish a pilot-ready version by 06/25 if we get the final pinned model artifacts and example payloads this week.
- Regarding doc showstoppers: propose we define a showstopper as any missing content that prevents a pilot engineer from completing an end-to-end integration (auth, model selection, inference example, and error handling). Anything else can be deferred to post-wide-release.

AtlasHealth: is there any documentation your team requires ahead of pilot beyond what Vanessa outlined? Any regulatory artifacts beyond SOC 2 evidence?

On the schedule: I recommend not committing to July 10 wide release unless Infra confirms latency SLOs and we complete the quickstart by 06/25. If those slip, push wide release by one sprint (2 weeks).

—Monica

Subject: Re: Enablement heatmap + release sequencing — clarify product asks and exception lanes

Vanessa / team,

On model pinning: serving only v2.1 for the pilot is doable but risky if we learn regressions at scale. My recommendation:
- Deploy v2.1 to pilot pool and configure an automatic fallback to v1.9 for any request that triggers a safety or correctness regression signature.
- Run a 2% canary to AtlasHealth traffic day one of pilot; if metrics are stable for 48 hours, increase to 25% then 100% over a week.

Infra work required: quantization profile for v2.1 (I estimate 2 engineer-weeks), and an automatic rollout/fallback pipeline. I'll own the infra plan but need Product to confirm the exact regression signatures we care about (latency, hallucination rate threshold, token cost ceiling).

Owners I propose: Marcus (infra rollout + fallback), Monica (SLO doc + quickstart QA), Lauren (customer webinars). If anyone objects, flag now.

Marcus

Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Enablement heatmap + release sequencing — clarify product asks and exception lanes

Thanks — I can take enablement delivery. A few practical items: 

- Webinar slots: propose June 27 10:00 PT and July 3 14:00 PT for the two sessions. Please confirm AtlasHealth availability.
- Quickstart distribution: I will prepare the single-page quickstart and a one-page troubleshooting KB. I need the final API examples and pinned model config by 06/22 to hit the June 25 pilot-ready doc date.
- Exception lane: documentation showstopper should be defined in the plan with concrete acceptance criteria (I agree with Monica). If docs are the only blocker at pilot handoff we keep pilot internal but continue webinar cadence.

Also: can we localize the quickstart into Spanish for AtlasHealth's EMEA team? That would add one week. If localization is required, propose we still pilot US customers first and schedule localized docs for the post-wide-release cadence.

Lauren

Subject: Re: Enablement heatmap + release sequencing — clarify product asks and exception lanes

All — I agree with the proposed owners and the conservative gating approach. I sketched a short mutual action plan below; I can take overall coordination: 

Mutual action plan (owner — due):
- Infra: quant profile + fallback pipeline (Marcus — 06/26)
- SLO page (Monica/Infra numbers — 06/22)
- Quickstart pilot doc (Lauren — 06/25)
- Webinars (Lauren — schedule requests sent to AtlasHealth by 06/15)
- Compliance check (AtlasHealth SOC evidence; Procurement loop to confirm contract terms — Procurement — 06/20)

If SOC evidence or any compliance gating item is not completed by 07/03, we hold wide release and extend the pilot window by two weeks. If the model shows correctness regressions during the 2% canary, we revert to v1.9 and pause rollout until a fix is validated.

Next steps: I will publish this MAP to a Google doc and share. Please reply with any edits; otherwise I will treat this as the agreed plan and book weekly 30-minute syncs starting 06/16.

—Aditya
